issues.description: Training loop never terminates cleanly when max_step is reached mid-epoch
issues.detail: The outer `while self.global_step < self.max_step` loop only checks between full `train()` calls, but `train()` runs `save_interval` batches regardless. There is no inner check, so global_step can overshoot max_step. The termination invariant `global_step <= max_step at loop boundary` is not maintained. State the invariant and add an inner check.

issues.description: Final checkpoint at max_step is never saved if loop exits before reaching the save block
issues.detail: Because `run()` saves only after `train()`+`valid()` complete a full save_interval window, the last partial window's progress can be lost. Worse, if `global_step` exceeds `max_step` inside train(), the while predicate becomes false and the loop exits without final save. Add an explicit terminal save outside the loop.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats uses SUM/world_size but averages NaNs and ignores per-rank batch counts
issues.detail: Loss/metric averaging assumes every rank processed an equal, non-empty batch. If one rank's iterator drains early or returns NaN, the global mean is silently corrupted. State the invariant: "each rank contributes one valid scalar per key per step." Consider weighting by sample count, or assert finiteness before reducing.

issues.description: Validation averaging is unweighted across variable-size batches
issues.detail: `sum(value)/len(value)` over per-batch means gives each batch equal weight regardless of token/sample count. The correct estimator for a dataset-level mean must weight by batch size. For an LM with variable sequence lengths this materially distorts reported perplexity/loss. State what quantity is being estimated, then choose the estimator.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery sort is O(n log n) on strings parsed with split; brittle to naming drift
issues.detail: `int(x.name.split("step_")[-1])` silently breaks if anyone adds a suffix like `step_1000_best`. Asymptotics are fine, but the parse is fragile and the invariant "directory name matches `step_<int>$`" is unstated. Use a regex with anchors and reject non-matches loudly. A literate comment naming the invariant would help future readers.

issues.description: train_dtype is a pure function but bound as method; precedence between bf16/fp16/amp undocumented
issues.detail: The cascade bf16 -> fp16 -> amp -> float32 encodes a priority that is not stated in a comment. A reader cannot tell whether simultaneously enabling bf16 and amp is an error or silently resolved. Either make it a free function and document the precedence as the loop invariant of the cascade, or validate mutual exclusivity up front.

review.summary: The trainer is UNDER-AUDITED at the loop level: the termination invariant linking `global_step`, `max_step`, and `save_interval` is never stated, and the code can both overshoot max_step and skip the final checkpoint. The distributed statistics reduction silently assumes equal, finite, equally-weighted contributions across ranks and batches — an asymptotically-OK / practically-wrong estimator for LM loss with variable-length sequences. Checkpoint discovery is correct but fragile, lacking a stated naming invariant. Overall: NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT and tightening of invariants; nothing here is asymptotically wrong, but several pieces are correct only under unstated preconditions that a careful reader cannot verify locally.
